title: The Three Little Pigs
originalTitle: The Story of the Three Little Pigs
sourceTitle: The Story of the Three Little Pigs
note: A new child-friendly adaptation. Unlike the historical source, the first two pigs escape to their sibling’s house and the wolf flees rather than being killed.

rights.basis: Source edition published before 1929 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: Three pigs stand beside houses of straw, sticks, and brick.
scenes: Three little pigs went out to build homes. The first chose straw because it was quick. The second chose sticks. The third carried bricks, one heavy armful at a time.
A wolf huffed and puffed the straw house down. The first pig ran to the stick house—but the wolf blew that one down too. Both pigs hurried to the brick house.
The wolf huffed. He puffed. He blew until he was dizzy, but the brick walls did not move.
The wolf tried the roof and slid toward the chimney. The pigs heard his claws and placed a great empty washtub below, then banged pots and pans as loudly as they could.
The startled wolf shot back up the chimney and ran away. The three pigs repaired the first two houses together—this time with strong walls and patient work.

pageArt.alt: Wolf huffs outside the brick house while the three pigs watch safely through a window.
The three pigs work together on strong brick homes in the English countryside.
